help.intro: The same nine prepositions take the accusative when they answer wohin? — where to? — that is, when something moves towards a place: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch. Die Katze springt unter das Bett. Ich hänge das Bild an die Wand. The verbs on this side are the verbs of putting: legen (lay flat), stellen (stand upright), setzen (sit down), hängen (hang up), and the verbs of going: gehen, fahren, kommen, springen. Each position verb from the last quiz has a movement partner — liegen/legen, stehen/stellen, sitzen/setzen, hängen/hängen — and the pair tells you the case. With ins (in das), ans (an das) and aufs (auf das) you have the contractions of this side.
help.tips[0].text: Something moves to a place: auf den Tisch, unter das Bett, an die Wand, in die Küche, ins Kino. Only the masculine changes visibly (den); die and das look like the nominative.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I put the lamp on the table.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We're going to the cinema and then into town.
help.tips[0].trap: the arrow rule: if you could draw an arrow of movement, it is the accusative. 'Ich gehe im Kino' says you are walking around inside the cinema.
help.tips[0].check.q: Heute Abend gehen wir ____ Theater. (We're going to the theatre tonight.)
help.tips[0].check.why: Going to the theatre is movement towards a place (wohin?), so in takes the accusative: in das → ins. im would mean you are already inside.
help.tips[0].visual.caption: An arrow: it moves there. Wohin? asks for the accusative.
help.tips[1].title: legen / stellen / setzen / hängen — the putting verbs
help.tips[1].text: liegen ↔ legen (lie / lay), stehen ↔ stellen (stand / put upright), sitzen ↔ setzen (sit / seat), hängen ↔ hängen (hang / hang up). The second of each pair takes an object and the accusative.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I lay the book on the table. — The book lies on the table.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: I hang the jacket in the wardrobe. — The jacket hangs in the wardrobe.
help.tips[1].check.q: Ich ____ das Handy auf den Tisch. (I put the phone down.)
help.tips[1].check.why: legen is the putting verb: it has an object and moves it, so it goes with the accusative den. liegen only says where something already is.
help.tips[2].title: The cat jumps
help.tips[2].text: Die Katze springt auf die Box — moving, accusative. The arrow A→ is the A of Akkusativ.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Where does the cat jump? – Onto the box.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The cat jumps onto the table.
help.tips[2].check.q: Wohin läuft der Hund? – Unter ____ Tisch. (der Tisch)
help.tips[2].check.why: Wohin? means movement — the arrow — so unter takes the accusative: der Tisch → den Tisch.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: At the weekend we're going to the countryside.
help.tips[3].check.why: sich setzen is movement, so an takes the accusative: an das → ans. am is the dative (where you already sit).
help.remember[0]: Wohin? — an arrow — accusative: auf den, in die, ins.
help.remember[1]: legen–stellen–setzen–hängen put things somewhere → accusative; liegen–stehen–sitzen–hängen say where they are → dative.
help.context.en: I'm tidying up: I put the books on the shelf and put the cup in the kitchen. I hang the jacket in the wardrobe, I put the shoes under the bed. Then I sit down on the sofa – done! Now the books lie on the shelf, the jacket hangs in the wardrobe, and I'm sitting on the sofa.
help.mistakes[0].why: legen moves the book: wohin? → accusative den.
help.mistakes[1].why: Going to a place is wohin?: ins.
help.hook: Put things somewhere and go places: draw an arrow of movement, and in, auf, an switch to the accusative — den, die, ins.
help.recall.known: From "Wechselpräpositionen: Wo?": the nine prepositions with the dative for a position.
help.recall.today: The same nine with the accusative, when something moves: the putting verbs legen, stellen, setzen, hängen.
help.table.caption: Put it there, then it is there
sentences[0].english: I put the book on the table.
sentences[0].why: legen moves the book somewhere (wohin?), so accusative: der → den Tisch.
sentences[1].english: The cat jumps under the bed.
sentences[1].why: Jumping TO a place: accusative — das stays das (das-words never change there).
sentences[2].english: I hang the picture on the wall.
sentences[2].why: Hanging it UP somewhere: accusative — die stays die.
sentences[3].why: Movement into: accusative — der → den Park.
sentences[4].english: Put the shoes in front of the door.
sentences[4].why: stellen puts them somewhere: accusative — vor die Tür.
sentences[5].english: I sit down next to the man.
sentences[5].why: Sitting DOWN somewhere is movement: accusative — neben den Mann.
sentences[6].english: I put the vase on the shelf.
sentences[6].why: stellen = movement: accusative — auf das Regal.
sentences[7].english: He hangs the clock above the door.
sentences[7].why: Hanging it up (wohin?): accusative — über die Tür.
sentences[8].why: Driving into town: accusative — in die Stadt.
sentences[9].english: The dog runs behind the tree and hides there.
sentences[9].why: Running TO behind the tree: accusative — hinter den Baum.
sentences[10].english: I put the letter between the books.
sentences[10].why: Placing it (wohin?): accusative plural stays die — zwischen die Bücher.
sentences[11].english: She puts the milk in the fridge.
sentences[11].why: Putting it in: accusative — in den Kühlschrank.
sentences[12].english: The child jumps into the water.
sentences[12].why: Jumping into: accusative — in das Wasser, das unchanged.
sentences[13].english: I sit down by the window.
sentences[13].why: Sitting down at it (movement): accusative — an das Fenster.
sentences[14].english: Put the chair in front of the desk.
sentences[14].why: stellen = placing: accusative — vor den Schreibtisch.
sentences[15].english: He puts the phone next to the plate.
sentences[15].why: legen = placing: accusative — neben den Teller.
sentences[16].english: Hang your jacket on the hook, please!
sentences[16].why: Hanging it onto: accusative — an den Haken.
sentences[17].english: The children put the presents under the Christmas tree.
sentences[17].why: legen = movement: accusative — unter den Weihnachtsbaum.
sentences[18].english: I put the flowers between the windows.
sentences[18].why: Placing them (wohin?): accusative plural die — zwischen die Fenster.
help.tips[0].title: Wohin? → Akkusativ: den / die / das
help.tips[3].title: ins, ans, aufs
